page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A4.Ax.Flex.32-512 is an Arm-based virtual machine instance utilizing the Ampere AmpereOne-M processor family. The server provides 64 dedicated physical cores running 64 vCPUs, with exactly one thread per core. The absence of simultaneous multithreading avoids noisy-neighbor contention across shared execution units. System memory is sized at 512.0 GB, delivering an allocation of 8.0 GB of RAM per core.

Hardware accelerators are absent, with a zero GPU count. The configuration includes no local NVMe storage, requiring all persistent data to rely on external network-attached block volumes. Networking provisioning includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. From a cost and architecture perspective, the single-threaded Arm64 core design yields high execution predictability and resource density relative to dual-threaded x86 alternatives, though workloads relying on x86-specific instruction sets cannot run without re-compilation or emulation.

With an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio and 64 dedicated cores, the VM.Standard.A4.Ax.Flex.32-512 configuration is suited for memory-intensive workloads that benefit from consistent single-threaded execution. Common deployments include in-memory databases, large-scale caching tiers, big data analytics engines, and containerized Arm-native enterprise backends.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A4.Ax.Flex.32-512 is an Arm-based instance built on the Ampere AmpereOne-M processor family. It features 64 dedicated physical cores and 64 vCPUs with a 1:1 core-to-thread ratio, eliminating hardware-level multithreading resource contention. The server provides 512.0 GB of system memory, establishing an 8.0 GB RAM per core ratio. There is no bundled local storage, meaning primary disk IOPS and storage capacity are provided through remote block storage volumes. The instance does not include graphics accelerators or specialized matrix coprocessors, but does include one complimentary public IPv4 address. Its balance of high memory density and dedicated execution cores makes the platform suitable for in-memory databases, distributed memory caching, big data processing pipelines, and large-scale Arm-native enterprise application servers.
